rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / THE STANDARD LIBRARY / CHAPTER 38

slides.title: Data and types
slides.main: Types describe the domain: tidy data, tidy project.

slides.title: dataclass
slides.main: Annotations in a dataclass describe fields, not check values.

body.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class User:
    name: str
    age: int = 18

u = User("Anna", 20)
print(u)
print(u == User("Anna", 20), User("Boris"))

slides.title: Which to choose
slides.main: Structure first: dataclass. Behavior first: class.

body.text: Many methods around a record? Time for a full class.

slides.title: Enum
slides.main: A typo in a member name fails at once; the editor suggests options.

body.text:
from enum import Enum

class Color(Enum):
    RED = 1
    GREEN = 2
    BLUE = 3

print(Color.RED, Color.RED.name, Color.RED.value)
print(Color(2), Color["BLUE"], list(Color))
print(Color.RED is Color(1))
try:
    Color(9)
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)

Color.RED RED 1
Color.GREEN Color.BLUE [<Color.RED: 1>, <Color.GREEN: 2>, <Color.BLUE: 3>]
True
9 is not a valid Color

slides.title: Enum variants
slides.main: Add methods to an enum: each member can do something.

body.text:
from enum import Enum, IntEnum, Flag, auto

class Status(str, Enum):
    NEW = "new"
    DONE = "done"
    def is_final(self):
        return self is Status.DONE

class Perm(Flag):
    R = auto()
    W = auto()
    X = auto()

rw = Perm.R | Perm.W
print(Status("done").is_final(), Status.NEW == "new")
print(rw, Perm.W in rw, Perm.X in rw)

class Level(IntEnum):
    LOW = 1
    HIGH = 3

print(Level.LOW < Level.HIGH, Level.HIGH + 1)

True True
Perm.R|W True False
True 4

slides.title: Type hints
slides.main: Python checks nothing: people, editors, analyzers read hints.

body.text:
def add(a: int, b: int = 0) -> int:
    return a + b

def first(items: list[str]) -> str | None:
    return items[0] if items else None

print(add(1, 2), first(["a"]), first([]))
print(add.__annotations__)
print(add("a", "b"))        # not checked!

slides.title: Why hints
slides.main: Honest docs, errors found before running, better editor help.

body.text: A static analyzer (mypy, pyright) spots a string where a number is needed.

slides.title: TypedDict, NamedTuple, Protocol
slides.main: A protocol is formal duck typing: any object with the right methods fits.

slides.title: match / case
slides.main: The _ pattern matches anything; put it last, or some values go unhandled.

body.text:
def run(cmd):
    match cmd:
        case ["go", int(n)]:
            return f"going to {n}"
        case ["say", *words]:
            return " ".join(words)
        case {"type": "quit"}:
            return "exit"
        case _:
            return "did not get it"

print(run(["go", 10]), run(["say", "a", "b"]), run({"type": "quit"}), run(5))
going to 10 a b exit did not get it

slides.title: copy and deepcopy
slides.main: Nested mutable data that must be independent needs deepcopy.

body.text:
import copy

a = [[1, 2], [3]]
shallow = copy.copy(a)
deep = copy.deepcopy(a)
a[0].append(99)
print(shallow[0], deep[0])
print(shallow is a, shallow[0] is a[0], deep[0] is a[0])
